C-SEC-SAVE-HANDLE.Summary: The sandboxed save/write boundary validates the target once with the M-010 fence and then mutates and opens the file by re-resolving path strings, so parallel path mutation inside the workspace can make a save land outside the sandbox. This change pins a fence-before-open invariant in the single shared writer — the last M-010 validation runs immediately before the only opening syscall, after all directory mutation, with no filesystem work in between — and pins the race shape with deterministic regression tests, while keeping allowed-symlink semantics and all existing denial behavior unchanged.
C-SEC-SAVE-HANDLE.Problem: Finding from the 2026-11 smart-review security run (task F-004, "save re-resolves the file path after the boundary check"): the write path re-resolves the target after the boundary check. Confirmed in current code. All mutating writers converge on write_validated_bytes (src-tauri/src/m013b/fs.rs:134-145): m010_security::check_path fences once (fs.rs:136), then fs::create_dir_all runs on the parent (fs.rs:138-140), then fs::File::create opens the validated path (fs.rs:141). Both steps after the fence re-resolve path strings through the kernel and follow symlinks introduced in between. The fence itself is correct at evaluation time (m010_security.rs:168-248, canonicalize_nearest_ancestor m010_security.rs:271-288), but the gap between evaluation and open is unguarded. Concrete windows for a local process with write access inside the workspace or an allowed ancestor: (a) plant the still-missing leaf as a symlink to an outside target between fence and create — File::create follows it and the saved bytes land outside; (b) swap a not-yet-existing directory component for an outward symlink between fence and create_dir_all — create_dir_all succeeds through the link and the create lands beyond the sandbox; (c) swap an existing directory component of the validated path to an outward symlink after the fence. Every save route is exposed because all writers funnel here: fs_write_inner (fs.rs:123, save-and-close path m001_save_close.rs:219, 464), fs_write_bytes_inner (fs.rs:128, document snapshot path m001_save_close.rs:356), fs_write_binary_inner (fs.rs:353). The document save additionally fences early for its ownership comparison (m001_save_close.rs:337-354), but the actual boundary remains the re-resolving writer. The sandbox root is defined by canonicalization at set time (m005_prefs.rs:345-369). Severity: medium — requires an active local writer racing Mark's save; consequence: attacker-placed bytes or clobbered files outside the user-chosen workspace.
C-SEC-SAVE-HANDLE.Relationship: Same smart-review security run family (commit be2f52f880bc) as C-SEC-STREAM-SCOPE (run F-001), C-SEC-EDIT-TARGETING and C-SEC-PAIR-REBIND. Builds on C-SEC-AUDIT-FIXES (nearest-existing-ancestor fencing in check_path), C-WINDOWS-SAVE-PIPELINE (permissive-root and \\?\ device-prefix comparison honesty) and C-METADATA-SAVE-SAFETY (the shared validated writer with in-place write_all/sync_all semantics). Finding-id discrepancy, flagged for the orchestrator: in security.findings.json of run be2f52f880bc the id F-004 carries key pull-request-defines-its-own-exposure-scan (a CI finding, unrelated) and no finding in that run describes the save-path TOCTOU; this spec is drafted from the task brief's inline finding description, which the code walk independently confirms (fs.rs:134-145). Re-verify the intended finding id before approval.

Goals.Goal: Fence-before-open invariant: the shared writer runs its final M-010 validation immediately before the only opening syscall, after create_dir_all and with no filesystem work in between; text, binary and document save callers all reach the disk through this one hardened boundary, and no caller opens a file through a path whose validation predates the last filesystem mutation it performs.

Race denial: a leaf or directory component planted or swapped during the window whose re-resolved canonical target leaves the canonical sandbox is denied with the existing MT_FS_PATH_DENIED error family; no bytes reach the outside target and no partial file appears at the requested path.

Allowed-symlink semantics unchanged: inward ancestor links, inward leaf links, missing-parent auto-creation, dangling-leaf denial, outward-ancestor denial and the permissive-root / Windows device-prefix rules keep their current behavior and tests green.

Deterministic race-shape regression tests pin both the denial and the allowance (injected-mutation test seam or an equally deterministic mechanism), and the module contract plus graph and verification surfaces state the invariant and the residual single-syscall window honestly.

Constraints.Constraint: Exact ObservedWriteScope below; m005_prefs.rs is reference-only (no behavioral change planned there), m010_security.rs keeps fence semantics (only contract/doc notes or a reused-helper export if needed), m001_save_close.rs changes only inside its save/write functions and tests.

src-tauri/src/m010_security.rs (fence unchanged; contract note / helper reuse if needed, plus its test module)
src-tauri/src/m005_prefs.rs (sandbox-root reference; test-only additions if an invariant pin needs it)

Constraints.Constraint: m010_security stays stdlib-only per its module contract; no new direct crate dependencies in this change (no libc / rustix / windows-sys promotion), even though those crates are already in Cargo.lock transitively.

Write semantics preserved: in-place write_all + sync_all, non-atomic (C-METADATA-SAVE-SAFETY), parent auto-creation, m047 bookmark rescue at the command layer untouched, no new IPC command ids, no renderer changes; denials reuse the existing error codes so renderer failure handling is unchanged.

Platform honesty, recorded so no later change claims more than std delivers: Rust std offers no held-descriptor final-component open on any desktop platform. On Unix, OpenOptionsExt exposes custom_flags but no O_NOFOLLOW constant (the flag value lives outside std and differs per unix); on Windows, custom_flags can pass FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT to the final component only, where the opened handle then refers to the reparse point itself (requiring a post-open not-a-reparse-point assertion) and intermediate components still resolve normally. The OS-true design (Linux openat2 with RESOLVE_BENEATH-style flags via libc/rustix — no std exposure, and RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS would reject the inward links this change must keep working; macOS per-component openat with O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY via libc; Windows per-component CreateFileW via windows-sys, where junctions and mount points are legitimate workspace features) is explicitly out of scope here; this change is the bounded first step and its residual race is the single kernel pathwalk between the last fence and create.

Repository artifacts stay English; module contracts, module maps and CHANGE_SUMMARY blocks in touched Rust files are synchronized; graph and verification references are updated with the change; no release actions.

NonGoals.NonGoal: The OS-level no-follow redesign: openat2 on Linux (libc/rustix), per-component openat with O_NOFOLLOW on macOS (libc), per-component CreateFileW with reparse-point policy on Windows (windows-sys), a dirfd-holding SecurityCtx and an M-010 dependency-contract change, plus per-hop symlink resolution policy to preserve inward links. Named as the follow-up direction with its own approval.

The inside-workspace ownership race in write_document_snapshot_inner (target swapped onto another owned document's path between the ownership comparison and the write) — integrity within the sandbox, not workspace escape.
The non-canonicalizing sandbox restore in m005_prefs restore_workspace — path-form honesty is already handled by device-prefix stripping; untouched.
Sibling findings of the same run: F-003 (HTML export read scope), F-005 (diff .before sidecar bypass) and the published F-004 (PR self-scanning) — separate changes.
Atomic save (temp file + rename) redesign — a C-METADATA-SAVE-SAFETY follow-up area, orthogonal to the fence-before-open invariant.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Race-shape regression, fails before the fix and passes after: with parallel path mutation injected deterministically between the fence and the create — a planted outward leaf symlink and a swapped outward ancestor directory — the write/save is refused with the MT_FS_PATH_DENIED family, the outside target's content is byte-for-byte unchanged, and no file appears at the requested path (finding checklist: parallel path mutation cannot make the save land outside the workspace).

Allowance regressions stay green unchanged: ancestor_inward_ok, symlink_inside_sandbox_allowed, write_creates_parent_dirs_when_missing, write_overwrites_existing_file, read_write_utf8_roundtrip, ancestor_dangling_leaf_refused, ancestor_existing_outward regression, the m010 ancestor_escape_* matrix, and the m001 save/snapshot suites (finding checklist: allowed symlinks still work).

Every mutating entry — mt_fs_write, mt_fs_write_binary, fs_write_inner, fs_write_bytes_inner, fs_write_binary_inner, the save-and-close write path and write_document_snapshot_inner — funnels through the single hardened writer, and no caller performs an un-fenced File::create on a fence-validated path.

The fs.rs module contract, the M-002/M-010 graph summaries and the V-M-002/V-M-010 verification surfaces state the fence-before-open invariant, the residual single-syscall window and the per-platform follow-up direction honestly.
grace lint with --change C-SEC-SAVE-HANDLE passes target and final assertions, and the four touched-module cargo suites stay green in CI on all desktop platforms.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: The race-shape denial test fails on pre-fix code and passes post-fix; the fence, symlink-allowance and save suites stay green; no renderer suite is touched so no npx command is expected (cargo --locked --offline follows the same registry discipline the run's F-012 asks of CI); final GRACE assertions and current-state integrity pass.

Assumptions.Assumption: The finding under remediation is the task brief's save-path re-resolution TOCTOU; the F-004 id mismatch in the run JSON is flagged in Relationship and re-verified by the orchestrator before approval.
Attacker model: a local process with write access inside the workspace or an allowed ancestor, racing Mark's save; no privilege escalation beyond that is claimed as fixed.

A cfg(test) injection seam inside the shared writer (a no-op hook between directory mutation and open) is acceptable contract surface; the plan may substitute an equally deterministic race-shape mechanism.
